# dec-gerber-rev — where the revision identifier actually lives, and whether "rev?" blocks fab

**Item:** decide whether the unresolved revision in the rev_b fabrication package is a real blocker or
a documentation nit, name every place a revision appears in a fab-visible artefact, and (per the
owner steer) give the least-effort fix. Also re-check the 36 HDI vias.
**Package under test:** `evidence/w2-da-gerbers/` — the rev_b package regenerated by wave 2
(11 Gerbers + `.gbrjob` + 7 Excellon files + 7 drill maps + `.pos`, 27 files).
**Board:** `repos/drone-arm/hardware/main/rev_b/main_rev_b.kicad_pcb`, SHA-256
`9B3BBA85C01AAC9E8365AF999F5231C3951E3428C37544A2B2CADC425F89953C` (unchanged before and after this
item — verified by `Get-FileHash` at start and end of `rev_identifier_probe.ps1`).
**Tool:** KiCad 9.0.7 (`kicad-cli.exe`, `python.exe` + `pcbnew`).
**Nothing was written into any repo and no git command was run.** All output is in this directory.

---

## 1. Verdict

**"rev?" is not a CAM blocker. It is a real traceability blocker, and it is the cheapest thing on the
whole board to fix.**

Two separate questions get conflated in the wave-2 wording "the rev field still reads unresolved":

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| Can a fab house cut, drill and plate this package without a revision string? | **Yes.** No CAM step consumes a revision. It is metadata. |
| Can anyone tell, from the files, whether a given package is rev_a or rev_b? | **No.** Both packages say `rev?`. §2.7. |

So the failure mode is not "the fab rejects the order". It is the one that already happened once in
this repo: two different boards, two packages, the same unresolved revision token, and no in-file
discriminator between them. Wave 1 hit exactly this (`evidence/fab-readiness/REPORT.md:60-83`).

And the fix costs **one line of metadata plus one re-export**, with geometry proven unchanged (§4).

---

## 2. Every place a revision identifier appears — complete inventory

The package has 27 files. Six classes of artefact could plausibly carry a revision. They do not
behave alike.

| # | artefact | field | current value | carry? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | board source, `.kicad_pcb` | `(title_block (rev ...))` | **section absent entirely** | — |
| 2 | `.gbrjob` | `GeneralSpecs.ProjectId.Revision` | **`rev?`** | yes |
| 3 | `.gbrjob` | `GeneralSpecs.ProjectId.Name` / `GUID` | `main_rev_b` / `6d61696e-5f72-…` | yes (from filename) |
| 4 | all 11 Gerbers **and all 7 drill-map Gerbers** | `%TF.ProjectId,<name>,<guid>,<rev>` | **`rev?`** in 18 of 18 files | yes |
| 5 | all 7 Excellon drill files | — | **no revision field exists** | no |
| 6 | `.pos` CSV | — | **no revision field exists** | no |
| 7 | silkscreen | `gr_text` on `F.SilkS` | **`REV-B FLIGHT CONTROL - DISTINCT FROM ESC`** | yes |

### 2.1 Title block — the section is *absent*, not empty

```
PS> Select-String -Path main_rev_b.kicad_pcb -Pattern 'title_block' | Measure-Object
Count: 0
```
The file goes `(version 20241229)` → `(generator "pcbnew")` → `(generator_version "9.0")` →
`(general (thickness 1.6) …)` at line 5 → `(setup` at line 38. There is no `(title_block …)` node at
all. `GetTitleBlock()` therefore returns four empty strings, which is what
`evidence/w2-da-gerbers/REPORT.md:59` reports — correct, but the stronger statement is that **no
revision was ever entered, and there is no placeholder to fill in**.

`rev?` is KiCad's own fallback token for "no revision given". Proof it is a fallback and not a stored
value: setting `(rev "B")` on a copy of the board makes both the `.gbrjob` and every `%TF.ProjectId`
read `B` (§4).

### 2.2 `.gbrjob`

`new/main_rev_b-job.gbrjob:14`:

```json
"ProjectId": { "Name": "main_rev_b", "GUID": "6d61696e-5f72-4657-965f-622e6b696361", "Revision": "rev?" }
```

The `GUID` is not random: its bytes visibly derive from the board file name (`6d 61 69 6e 5f 72 …` is
`"main_r"…`; the copy named `main_rev_b_revB` produced `…625f72657642`, i.e. `"b_revB"`). Both `Name`
and `GUID` are therefore file-name-derived, not title-block-derived — **measured, not inferred**: the
copy in §4 changed both, and would have changed the *project identity* had I renamed the board instead
of editing its title block. That is why the fix belongs in the title block.

### 2.3 Gerber X2 `%TF.ProjectId` — 18 files, not just the job file

Wave 2 wrote "Nothing inside the package identifies it as rev_b except the filename"
(`w2-da-gerbers/REPORT.md:277-280`). That is **wrong in one respect**: the revision token is embedded
in every Gerber's X2 attribute block — just with the unresolved value.

```
%TF.ProjectId,main_rev_b,6d61696e-5f72-4657-965f-622e6b696361,rev?*%
```

`grep -i rev` over every produced file (`rev_probe_output.txt`) finds it in **11 Gerbers + 7
drill-map Gerbers = 18 files**, plus the `.gbrjob`. So the revision has 19 carriers, all reading the
same wrong token.

### 2.4 Drill file headers — no revision field exists at all

Every `.drl` header is only:

```
M48
; DRILL file {KiCad 9.0.7} date 2026-11-14T18:49:38+0530
; FORMAT={-:-/ absolute / metric / decimal}
; #@! TF.CreationDate,2026-11-14T18:49:38+05:30
; #@! TF.GenerationSoftware,Kicad,Pcbnew,9.0.7
; #@! TF.FileFunction,Plated,1,2,Blind
```

No `TF.ProjectId`, no title, no rev. Setting `(rev "B")` leaves every `.drl` byte-identical except the
timestamp (`rev_probe_output.txt`, "Excellon headers"). KiCad's Excellon writer simply does not emit
project identity.

**The asymmetry is worth stating plainly:** the drill *map* Gerber carries `rev?`, but the drill *data*
the drill operator actually loads does not. The file that makes holes is revision-blind.

### 2.5 `.pos` — no revision field exists at all

`gerbers/main_rev_b-all-pos.csv:1` is `Ref,Val,Package,PosX,PosY,Rot,Side`, 161 data rows. Identical
header with `rev "B"` set. KiCad 9's CSV position exporter has no revision column and no comment
block.

### 2.6 Silkscreen — the revision *is* on the physical board

`main_rev_b.kicad_pcb:29528-29538`:

```
(gr_text "REV-B FLIGHT CONTROL - DISTINCT FROM ESC"
    (at 70 2.5 0)
    (layer "F.SilkS")
    (effects (font (size 1.5 1.5) (thickness 0.18))))
```

It is plotted. Verified two ways (`silk_rev_check.py` → `silk_rev_check.json`):

| layer | F.SilkS stroke segments | segments in the 1.5 mm band y ∈ [1,4] mm | x span of that band |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| package as exported | 562 | **256** | 43.464 – 96.607 mm (53.14 mm) |
| same board with that one `gr_text` deleted | 306 | **0** | — |

The band is exactly 1.5 mm tall (y 1.685 – 3.185 mm) and 53.14 mm wide, which is what a 40-character
1.5 mm string looks like, and removing the string removes exactly those 256 segments
(`del_test/no_rev_text-F_Silkscreen.gto`). **The board says REV-B on its own face.**

> This contradicts `fab-readiness/REPORT.md:141` ("no silk revision string") and the "nothing except
> the filename" clause of `w2-da-gerbers/REPORT.md:277`. See §6.

### 2.7 The stale package says `rev?` too — the actual defect

`repos/drone-arm/hardware/main/pcb-gerbers-1/` (the 75 × 50 mm rev_a board):
`main-job.gbrjob` `"Revision": "rev?"`, and every layer
`%TF.ProjectId,main,6d61696e-2e6b-4696-9361-645f70636258,rev?*%`.

So the repo holds **two structurally different boards that both declare `rev?`**. Neither package can
falsify the other; only the filename and (for rev_b, once it is in the repo) the silkscreen text
distinguish them.

---

## 3. What a fab or assembly house actually reads

Split by who reads it, and labelled honestly: the CAM-behaviour statements are industry practice, not
a measurement against a named house's ingest (UNVERIFIED, §7).

| field | read by CAM / assembly? | why |
|---|---|---|
| Gerber geometry, `%TF.FileFunction`, `%TF.FilePolarity` | **Yes, mandatory** | Layer identity. `FileFunction` is how a CAM front-end knows which file is L1 copper vs the profile — and, in the drill files, `Plated,1,2,Blind` is how it knows a sub-stack exists. |
| `.gbrjob`: `Size`, `LayerNumber`, `BoardThickness`, `Finish`, `MaterialStackup`, `DesignRules` | **Yes** | Quoting and DFM. This is the file that makes the order quotable without opening 11 Gerbers. |
| `.gbrjob`: `ProjectId.Revision` | **Cosmetic** | No CAM step branches on it. It is a label. |
| Gerber `%TF.ProjectId` revision token | **Cosmetic** | X2 attributes are parsed mainly for `FileFunction`/`FilePolarity`/`CreationDate`. |
| Excellon headers | **No rev field exists** | Nothing to read. |
| `.pos` header | **No rev field exists** | Assembly houses key on the filename, the BOM and the purchase order. |
| **Silkscreen `REV-B`** | **Yes — by humans** | The only revision marking on the physical part. It is what an assembly operator, an AOI recipe owner, a QA inspector and the customer's incoming inspection actually look at. |

What a fab really keys on, in order: the purchase order → the zip/file names → the fab drawing (which
**does not exist**: `fab-readiness/REPORT.md:148`, checklist line 34 MISSING) → the `.gbrjob`. The
revision string is nowhere in that chain.

**Consequence for the decision:** an unresolved `rev?` does not stop a build. A package that cannot be
told apart from a *different, 75 × 50 mm board* in the same tree does stop a *correct* build. The
board's own silk already solves the human half of that. The metadata half is one line away.

---

## 4. Minimum-effort fix (measured, not proposed)

Owner steer: fab burden is free, design effort is precious; part swaps and constraint edits before
copper, copper before stackup. The revision fix is *cheaper than all three* — it is metadata, and I
proved it changes no geometry.

`rev_identifier_probe.ps1` does exactly this, entirely inside this evidence directory:

1. copy the board to `work/main_rev_b_revB.kicad_pcb` (repo hash unchanged, before and after);
2. insert into the **copy**:
   ```
   (title_block
       (title "drone-arm flight controller main board")
       (date "2026-11-14")
       (rev "B")
       (company "engineering-portfolio-audit"))
   ```
3. re-export with the identical wave-2 `kicad-cli` flags into `revB_export/`;
4. diff every field.

Result:

| artefact | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `.gbrjob` `ProjectId.Revision` | `"rev?"` | `"B"` |
| `%TF.ProjectId` (18 files) | `…,rev?*%` | `…,B*%` |
| `.drl` headers | — | unchanged (timestamp only) |
| `.pos` header | — | unchanged |
| **copper / mask / silk / paste / profile geometry** | — | **identical in 11 of 11 layers** |

The geometry claim is not an assertion: after stripping `%TF` lines and the `G04 … date …` comment, all
eleven layers are line-for-line equal to the wave-2 package (`body_identical_except_timestamp=True`
for `F_Cu`, `In1_Cu`, `In2_Cu`, `B_Cu`, `Edge_Cuts`, `F_Silkscreen`, `F_Mask`, `B_Mask`, `F_Paste`,
`B_Paste`, `B_Silkscreen`).

**So the minimum-effort, physical-fidelity-preserving answer is:**

1. **One metadata line**: add `(rev "B")` (plus title/date/company, same edit) to the title block.
2. **One re-export**: no copper move, no stackup change, no constraint change, no part swap. Severity
   class **RE-SPIN** in the existing scheme (`fab-readiness/REPORT.md:55`), which is the cheapest class
   that exists.
3. **One hygiene action**: get the rev_a package out of the path a builder would reach for, or rename
   it to say rev_a. Both packages reading `rev?` is what made the wave-1 mix-up possible in the first
   place. This is the step that actually removes the risk; steps 1–2 only make the *new* package
   self-identifying.
4. **Nothing to do on silk** — `REV-B` is already there and already plotted (§2.6).

Two caveats: use `rev "B"`, not `"rev_b"`, so the string stays short and unambiguous against the
directory name `rev_b/`; and do **not** rename the `.kicad_pcb` — that changes `ProjectId.Name` *and*
the `GUID` (§2.2), which is a bigger change than the field being fixed.

## 5. HDI vias — count confirmed, and the count is not the whole story

### 5.1 Count

`hdi_via_probe.py` → `hdi_via.json`, from `pcbnew` directly (not from the Gerbers):

| span | 0.100 mm drill | 0.300 mm drill | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| F.Cu → In1.Cu (blind) | 14 | — | 14 |
| In1.Cu → In2.Cu (buried) | 10 | — | 10 |
| F.Cu → In2.Cu (blind) | 3 | — | 3 |
| In2.Cu → B.Cu (blind) | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| In1.Cu → B.Cu (blind) | 4 | — | 4 |
| **blind/buried** | **33** | **3** | **36** |
| F.Cu → B.Cu (through) | — | 305 | 305 |
| **all vias** | | | **341** |

This agrees exactly with the drill files (14+3+10+4+2 = 33 hits at 0.100 mm; 3 at 0.300 mm in
`in2-back.drl`) and with `w2-da-gerbers/REPORT.md:161-181`. `boardfacts` counts 33 at 0.100 mm — the
report's §6 table is internally inconsistent with its own drill table when it prints "36 … mostly
0.100".

### 5.2 The part that changes the decision: 17 of the 36 are not manufacturable at 0.1 mm

Aspect ratio computed from the board's own stackup (`main_rev_b.kicad_pcb:38-97`: F.Cu 0.035 /
prepreg 0.200 / In1 0.035 / **core 1.040** / In2 0.035 / prepreg 0.200 / B.Cu 0.035, sum 1.60 mm) and
the drill table:

| span | hole depth (mm) | drill | aspect ratio | vias | makeable? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| In2.Cu → B.Cu | 0.200 | 0.300 | 0.67 | 3 | yes |
| F.Cu → In1.Cu | 0.200 | 0.100 | 2.00 | 14 | laser regime, at/over the usual envelope |
| In2.Cu → B.Cu | 0.200 | 0.100 | 2.00 | 2 | laser regime, at/over the usual envelope |
| **In1.Cu → In2.Cu** | **1.040** | **0.100** | **10.4** | **10** | **no** |
| **F.Cu → In2.Cu** | **1.275** | **0.100** | **12.75** | **3** | **no** |
| **In1.Cu → B.Cu** | **1.275** | **0.100** | **12.75** | **4** | **no** |

*Mechanical* drilling has an industry floor around 0.15–0.20 mm, so 0.1 mm is laser-only; *laser* depth
is limited to roughly 0.1–0.15 mm, so 1.040 mm and 1.275 mm are not laser-reachable either. **17 vias
therefore have no process route at 0.1 mm on this stackup** — this is arithmetic from the board's own
thicknesses, not a supplier opinion (the supplier envelope itself is UNVERIFIED, §7).

That is a stronger finding than "fab burden is acceptable". The owner steer says fab burden is free;
it does not say physically unrealisable geometries are free. The 19 remaining (0.67 and 2.00 ratios)
are ordinary HDI-lite burden and are accepted without argument under the steer.

What the data suggests about intent: **13 of the 36 sit inside a pad** (via-in-pad, refdes
`U10.4/12/18/22/27`, `U40.4/7`, `R10.2`, `R32.2`) — the fanout of the QFN-80 / QFN-40 region. So the
designer was chasing fine-pitch escape, and 0.1 mm was chosen for room, not for any electrical reason.

### 5.3 Are any of them electrically necessary at 0.1 mm?

No. Evidence:

- 36 vias on **14 distinct nets**, all signal: `/LSM_INT1`, `/GNSS_RX`, `/RF_MOSI`, `/RF_MISO`,
  `/RF_SCLK`, `/RF_GPIO0`, `/RF_GPIO2`, `/RF_RESET_N`, `/PA_EN`, `/HGM`, `/SENS_SCLK`,
  `/RP2354B MCU/USB_DP_MCU`, `/915 MHz RF/VDD_CC112`, and **one** `/3V3`.
- One `/3V3` via is not a current path anyone would size at 0.1 mm (it is one via in a plane-connected
  net, and 305 through vias at 0.3/0.35 mm already bond that net).
- The only 0.1 mm-specific electrical argument would be via inductance. At 915 MHz the difference
  between a 0.1 mm and a 0.3 mm barrel is on the order of **1 nH** — immaterial against the 50 Ω
  geometry work in the wave-1 RF items, and no net here is a matched-line launch.

So: **standard 0.2–0.3 mm vias do the same electrical job.** The 0.1 mm is a density decision.

### 5.4 What conversion costs, measured

`hdi_via_probe.py` also asks, for each of the 36: if this became a through via, does any *foreign-net*
track on In1 or In2 fall inside the needed clearance?

- 8 of the 36 would collide at their present 0.3 mm pad — and **all 8 are in the makeable classes**
  (0.67 or 2.00). So the vias that can stay, can stay; every via that must move is currently clear of
  foreign copper down to 0.283 mm.
- Of the 17 unmakeable ones, against the board's 0.125 mm rule
  (`main_rev_b-job.gbrjob` `DesignRules` `PadToTrack 0.125`):

| through-via target | pad | clearance needed | of the 17 that clear it |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 0.30 mm drill | 0.60 mm | 0.425 mm | **5** |
| 0.20 mm drill | 0.45 mm | 0.350 mm | **7** |
| 0.20 mm drill | 0.40 mm | 0.325 mm | **9** |

So conversion is *not* free: 8–12 of the 17 need inner-layer track nudges of 0.05–0.14 mm
(worst: `/LSM_INT1` In1→In2 at 0.283 mm, `/GNSS_RX` at 0.325 mm). Per the steer's ordering that is
**copper moves**, which rank below stackup changes but above constraint edits.

**Conclusion under the steer.**
- The 19 makeable vias: **accept the fab burden**, no change (steer: fab burden is free).
- The 17 unmakeable ones: the file's own span assignment has to change. Cheapest physically faithful
  route is **convert them to 0.2 mm-drill through vias** (a via-property edit) plus ≤0.14 mm nudges on
  In1/In2 tracks for the ~10 that need it. That beats the only alternative — rebuilding the stackup as
  a thin-core HDI (core 1.04 → ~0.1 mm, i.e. sequential lamination with a different dielectric
  schedule), which the steer ranks last.
- Do **not** simply re-export and hope: as generated, five drill files demand holes no process can
  make. That is a physical infeasibility, not a burden.

> NOTE: the `2.00` class (16 vias, 0.1 mm through 0.200 mm prepreg) is at or beyond the usual laser
> aspect envelope. "Acceptable burden under the steer" is a *budget* statement, not a process
> guarantee — the supplier must confirm. See §7.

## 6. Corrections

### 6.1 BOARD CORRECTION — line 166 (and the same phrase on line 156)

`AGENT_BOARD.md:166` reads *"Accept 36 HDI 0.1 mm vias, or re-route to standard vias."* and line 156
*"Also 36 HDI 0.1 mm vias and 84 nets routed on a solid In1 plane."*

The **36** is confirmed. The **"0.1 mm"** is not: it is **33 at 0.100 mm + 3 at 0.300 mm**
(`hdi_via.json`; corroborated by `in2-back.drl` tool table `T1C0.100` / `T2C0.300`). More
importantly, "accept 36 HDI vias" is not a decision that can be taken as stated, because **17 of the
36 are not drillable at 0.1 mm on this stackup** (§5.2) — the decision is *"accept the 19, convert the
17"*, not *"accept all 36"*.

### 6.2 `w2-da-gerbers/REPORT.md` — two repairs

- `:277-280` "Nothing inside the package identifies it as rev_b except the filename." **Partly wrong.**
  The revision token is in 18 Gerber files (`%TF.ProjectId`) and the job file — just with the value
  `rev?`. What is true is that nothing in the package says **rev_b**, and that the F.SilkS text does
  say **REV-B** (§2.6).
- `:59` "Title block title/revision/date/company all empty." Correct but understated: there is **no
  `title_block` node at all** (§2.1).

### 6.3 `fab-readiness/REPORT.md` — one repair

- `:141` checklist line 28: "no silk revision string". **Wrong.** F.SilkS carries
  `REV-B FLIGHT CONTROL - DISTINCT FROM ESC` at `(70, 2.5)`, 1.5 mm text, and it is in the plotted
  Gerber (256 stroke segments, proved by removing it in `del_test/`). The line's *rating* (FAIL) is
  still right for a different reason — the title block and gbrjob carry `rev?` — but the stated
  evidence is false.

### 6.4 What stands

The re-exported package itself: 11 Gerbers, Edge_Cuts 140.000 × 100.000 mm, 7 Excellon files with
369 hits, 161-row `.pos`, 36 blind/buried vias, gbrjob Size 140.15 × 100.15 / 1.6 / ENIG. All
re-confirmed here, none re-derived as new.

---

## 7. UNVERIFIED

1. **No fab house was asked.** Which fields a given house's CAM front-end ingests is industry
   practice, stated as such; I did not submit this package to a house or read its DFM output.
2. **Laser/microvia process envelope.** The 10.4:1 and 12.75:1 ratios are arithmetic from the board's
   own stackup and are not physically drillable by any route I know of. The 2.00:1 class and the
   0.100/0.300 mm diameter floors are *typical* capability numbers, not a supplier's confirmation.
3. **Through-via conversion, outer layers.** `hdi_via_probe.py` checks clearance to foreign copper on
   **In1/In2 only**. A through via lands pads on F.Cu and B.Cu as well; those clearances, and mask
   openings, were not checked. The "5 / 7 / 9 of 17 clear" figures are inner-layer-only.
4. **Via-in-pad count.** 13 = via centre inside a pad bounding box of the same net. That is a
   conservative test (a bbox, not the pad shape) and it does not check the mask/print implications of
   via-in-pad, which would need resin fill and planarisation — a fab burden, not a measured cost here.
5. **`rev "B"` has been applied to a copy only.** No repo file was edited; applying it, re-exporting
   and re-running the wave-2 validation is the next owner action, not something this item performed.
6. **`rev?` is KiCad's documented fallback** — I observed it in two independent boards with no title
   block and its replacement by `B` when the field is set. I did not read KiCad source to confirm the
   literal is hard-coded.

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File E:\engineering-portfolio-audit\evidence\dec-gerber-rev\rev_identifier_probe.ps1
& 'C:\Program Files\KiCad\9.0\bin\python.exe' E:\engineering-portfolio-audit\evidence\dec-gerber-rev\hdi_via_probe.py
& 'C:\Program Files\KiCad\9.0\bin\python.exe' E:\engineering-portfolio-audit\evidence\dec-gerber-rev\silk_rev_check.py
```
